title: Foundations: Country Rock - The Complete Guide
summary: What Country Rock is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Country Rock songs: Country-rock fused California folk-rock with Bakersfield twang: the Byrds, the Flying Burrito Brothers, and the Eagles made hippies and cowboys share a stage.

History: The Byrds' Sweetheart of the Rodeo (1968) and Gram Parsons's work invented it; the Eagles (1972–76) made it the biggest sound in America.

How the songs work: Country Rock favors the keys of G, D, A, E. Common forms include Verse-chorus with pedal-steel breaks; Harmony-stacked choruses. Players should master pedal steel over rock drums first, then stacked california harmonies. Capo 2 for jangly country-rock.

title: Country Rock Etude No. 1: Eagles vi–IV–I–V
summary: An original Country Rock study in D drilling stacked california harmonies.
body:
This original etude isolates the 'Eagles vi–IV–I–V' progression in the key of D — the changes Country Rock players must know cold.

CHART:
Dm | A# | F | C

FORM: harmony-stacked choruses.

PRACTICE: loop the chart slowly, adding stacked california harmonies once the changes are clean. Then transpose with the included program and drill it in all twelve keys — the Country Rock player's rite of passage.

title: Hotel California - Country Rock Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Hotel California by Eagles (1976).
body:
Hotel California — Eagles, 1976. The country-rock epic.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of A):
A | D | E | A

This study chart uses the 'Burrito I–IV–V' progression, the Country Rock workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: verse-chorus with pedal-steel breaks. Listen for telecaster-meets-rickenbacker jangle — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Country Rock pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let telecaster-meets-rickenbacker jangle. Capo 2 for jangly country-rock. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
